chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Abdullah al-Barqi and Abu Talib, from Bakr ibn Muhammad, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
O Allah, You are my reliance in every worry,
and You are my hope in every difficulty, and You are for me in every matter that befalls me, a Trustworthy and a Resource.

How many worries are there such that the heart weakens from them, and plans become scarce regarding them, and the near and far ones abandon them, and the enemies gloat with them, and the affairs exhaust me in them.
I revealed it to You and complained of it to You, turning away from those besides You. Therefore, relieve it, remove it, and suffice for me regarding it.
For You are the Patron of every bounty and the Companion of every need, and the End-point of every desire. So, for You is abundant praise, and for You is the overflowing favor.
ai.seo_question: What is the supplication for reliance on God in times of difficulty?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this supplication (du'a) from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) serves as a comprehensive model for seeking divine aid during calamities, emphasizing total reliance (tawakkul) on Allah when human efforts and social support fail. It highlights the theological concept of shifting from self-reliance to absolute dependence on God, acknowledging Him as the ultimate source of relief and sufficiency. This text is frequently cited in Shia devotional practices to cultivate spiritual resilience and gratitude during times of hardship.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Abu Abdullah Al Barqy, and Abu Talib, from Bakr Bin Muhammad, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘(Say), ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>!

You<sup>azwj</sup> are my reliance during every worry, and You<sup>azwj</sup> are my hope during every difficulty, and Your<sup>azwj</sup> are for me during every matter which descends with me, as a Trustworthy and the Resource.

And how many worries were such that the heart was weakened from it, and the plans were scarce with regards to it, and the end near ones and the far ones abandoned from it, and the enemies gloated with it, and the life-time was exhausted in it.
I revealed it to You<sup>azwj</sup> and complained of it to You<sup>azwj</sup>, turning away from the ones besides You<sup>azwj</sup>.

Therefore, Relieve it and Remove it and Suffice for it, for You<sup>azwj</sup> are the Patron of every Bounty and a Companion of every need, and the End-point of every desire. So, for You<sup>azwj</sup> is the abundant Praise, and for You<sup>azwj</sup> is the extra Favours (to Grant)’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from abu ‘Abd Allah al-Barqi and abu Talib from Bakr ibn Muhammad from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
O Lord, You are my trustee in every distressful condition.
You are my hope in all suffering, You are for me in all of my problems, (You are) my trustee and my resources.
How many were the distressful conditions wherein the heart weakened, patience ran thin, people near left out and the enemies rejoiced all matters were exhausted?

You assisted me in the matters that I had brought before You and complained about them to You, turning away from everyone besides You and You changed it into happiness, removed the hardships and sufficed it (in its removal).
You are the patron of all blessings, the provider of all help, the end of all interests, all praise belongs to You a great deal and thanks to You in addition.”
